Key Objective: Ensure the debtor understands the factors causing financial distress and explores all viable alternatives to bankruptcy.

Required Actions (Inferred): Consumer must complete a session within  $180$  days before filing, provide full financial disclosure, and submit the certificate to the court.

Key Objective: Teach financial management skills to ensure a successful financial fresh start and bridge the gap to permanent stability.
Implementation Method: Minimum  $2$ -hour instructional course (or  $40$ -hour extended curriculum) covering budgeting, credit use, and behavioural shifts.
Target Audience: Bankruptcy filers who have filed their case but not yet received a discharge.

Required Actions (Inferred): Complete the course after filing but within  $60$ - $90$  days of the creditors' meeting and file the certificate with the court.

Key Objective: Screen out debtors with the ability to repay a portion of their debts to prevent 'abuse' of Chapter 7 liquidation.

Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Increases payments to unsecured creditors by funneling capable debtors into Chapter 13 repayment plans.
Required Actions (Inferred): Debtors must provide detailed financial records and tax returns to calculate net income; courts must dismiss or convert cases where abuse is presumed.

Key Objective: Consolidate and repay debts through a structured, informal negotiation outside of the court system.
Implementation Method: Working with a credit counselling agency to set up an accelerated payment plan often involving lower interest rates.
Target Audience: Individuals with high credit card debt who wish to avoid the stigma of formal bankruptcy.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Avoidance of bankruptcy court records, potential interest rate breaks, and improved mental well-being.
Required Actions (Inferred): Consumer must agree to close accounts, make a single monthly payment to the agency, and strictly follow a spending tracker/budget.

Key Objective: Heal financial shame, deconstruct harmful money scripts, and identify the origin of avoidance behaviours.
Implementation Method: Interdisciplinary approach mapping key financial memories and emotions to foster radical self-compassion.
Target Audience: Individuals experiencing bankruptcy-related stigma, chronic money stress, or financial trauma.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Reduced anxiety, cessation of avoidance behaviours, and transition to proactive, healthy financial planning.
Required Actions (Inferred): Consumer must honestly reflect on past financial trauma, track money triggers in a journal, and participate in guided reframing exercises.

Key Objective: Ensure credit report accuracy to prevent score suppression and verify a clean financial slate.
Implementation Method: Requesting free reports from Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion roughly  $90$  days after discharge to verify  $\$0$  balances.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Corrected credit profile, prevention of illegal collection of discharged debt, and quantification of progress.
Required Actions (Inferred): Visit annualcreditreport.com, verify discharged debts show a zero balance, and mail formal dispute letters for any inaccuracies.

Key Objective: Identify and avoid deceptive high-interest traps and aggressive subprime marketing.
Implementation Method: Instruction on calculating Annual Percentage Rate (APR) and recognising red flags like 'packing', 'loan flipping', or junk fees.
Target Audience: Post-bankruptcy dischargees and vulnerable borrowers targeted by aggressive subprime lenders.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Building an 'immune system' against financial exploitation and protection of home equity.
Required Actions (Inferred): Compare quotes from at least  $3$  lenders, ensure fees do not exceed  $1\%$  of the loan, and use APR calculators to compare costs.

Key Objective: Establish a foundational framework for balanced budgetary allocation and simplified income management.
Implementation Method: Allocate  $50\%$  of take-home pay to needs,  $30\%$  to discretionary wants, and  $20\%$  to savings/debt reduction.
Target Audience: General consumers and individuals seeking a robust post-bankruptcy financial structure.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Maintenance of essential stability, consistent savings growth, and creation of a buffer against crises.
Required Actions (Inferred): Calculate net monthly income, categorise all expenses, and automate a  $20\%$  transfer to a separate savings account.

Key Objective: Enforce hard spending boundaries and curb overspending through physical or digital categorisation.
Implementation Method: Dividing income into labelled envelopes for specific categories; spending must cease when an envelope is empty.
Target Audience: Beginners or those who struggle with the abstract nature of digital transactions and credit card use.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Creates a 'pain of paying' leading to conscious spending, real-time accountability, and adherence to limits.
Required Actions (Inferred): Withdraw physical cash monthly (or set up digital sub-accounts), label envelopes, and strictly stop spending once empty.

Strategy or Concept: Credit Builder Loans and Secured Cards
Key Objective: Re-establish a positive credit history and build savings when traditional credit is unavailable.
Implementation Method: Lender holds 'borrowed' money in a CD or requires a refundable cash deposit to serve as a credit limit.
Target Audience: Individuals with poor or no credit history seeking to improve their FICO score post-bankruptcy.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Improvement of payment history ( $35\%$  of FICO score) and creation of a lump sum of savings or unsecured credit access.
Required Actions (Inferred): Deposit  $150$ - $380$  GBP ( $200$ - $500$  USD) as collateral, use for small purchases, and pay the balance in full by the due date.

Strategy or Concept: Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) Accounts
Key Objective: Allow people with disabilities to save for qualified expenses without losing eligibility for means-tested public benefits.
Implementation Method: Establishment of a tax-advantaged savings account where the designated beneficiary is the account owner.
Target Audience: Individuals with significant disabilities that began before age  $26$ .
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Financial resilience and ability to cover long-term health costs while maintaining SSI and Medicaid.
Required Actions (Inferred): Individuals must select a state-run plan, contribute up to  $14,000$  USD annually ( $2017$  limit), and spend on qualified expenses.

Key Objective: Assign every unit of income a specific task before it is spent to dictate future stability.
Implementation Method: Mastering the mechanics of tracking every unit of inflow and outflow to ensure total allocation.
Target Audience: Post-bankruptcy clients transitioning from credit-dependent to cash-based models.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Permanent financial sovereignty and elimination of credit dependency.
Required Actions (Inferred): Consumer must rigorously track all daily spending and reconcile accounts to zero at the start of each month.

Key Objective: Manage irregular or unstable income to prevent 'boom and bust' cycles.
Implementation Method: Constructing a budget based on the lowest-earning month of the previous year.
Target Audience: Gig economy workers or seasonal earners post-bankruptcy.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Stabilised cash flow and protection against leaner months.
Required Actions (Inferred): Consumer must review  $12$  months of past earnings and open a 'buffer account' for surplus income.

Key Objective: Move away from stigmatising 'autonomy-based' laws toward responsive structures that support individual resilience.
Implementation Method: Removing stigmatising provisions like the means test and creating separate bankruptcy chapters for 'uncontrollable debt'.
Target Audience: Debtors facing financial crises due to medical emergencies, job loss, or divorce.
Associated Benefits or Outcomes: Reduced psychological burden, lower suicide risk, and a more effective 'fresh start'.
Required Actions (Inferred): Legislators must draft code revisions focusing on debt source; judiciary should be granted more discretion to waive hurdles.
